CC @ericstj

We've had other cases like this that we try to fix because they often represent some real edge-cases or faulty in the logic in the generator.

@eerhardt are you blocked here, or can you create a proxy type for the purposes of binding that wraps the real type you're trying to bind?

> FYI @drewnoakes - who added this call in the Dashboard. I didn't see any tests for it, nor docs. So I'm wondering if we really need it in the .NET Aspire Dashboard.

It was added to give more control over SSL options when using certificates to secure the resource service. I'm not aware of anyone who is actually using certificates for this connection internally, and use of `Dashboard:ResourceServiceClient:Ssl` is optional. Indeed it's not documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/aspire/fundamentals/dashboard/configuration?tabs=bash#resources, though arguably it should be.

All that to say, if it's significantly helpful to remove that configuration binding, I wouldn't expect much pushback.

> All that to say, if it's significantly helpful to remove that configuration binding, I wouldn't expect much pushback.

I don't think removing it from the dashboard affects this bug either way. This is a situation that causes the Configuration Binder source generator to emit uncompilable code, which should be fixed. It isn't critical to fix it right now, since the Dashboard doesn't need to use the source generator. But in the future I can imagine it may want to.
I agree, this need to be fixed in the source gen anyway.

review_comments: Can you explain all these conditions?  I only understand the first, why the others?

`complexType is not CollectionSpec` we have special handling to the collections so we should not change how we do it especially it should work in most cases. look at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/e4f93dbee0bc3f17f5ac2fad34e75f38865e866d/src/libraries/Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration.Binder/gen/Emitter/CoreBindingHelpers.cs#L1146 for more details.

`((ObjectSpec)complexType).InstantiationStrategy == ObjectInstantiationStrategy.ParameterizedConstructor)` is needed because if it is different ObjectInstantiationStrategy value means we can still create and handle the object. look at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/e4f93dbee0bc3f17f5ac2fad34e75f38865e866d/src/libraries/Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration.Binder/gen/Emitter/CoreBindingHelpers.cs#L1170 to see that.

`_typeIndex.GetEffectiveTypeSpec(complexType).IsValueType` can be handled too, https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/e4f93dbee0bc3f17f5ac2fad34e75f38865e866d/src/libraries/Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration.Binder/gen/Emitter/CoreBindingHelpers.cs#L933 shows what we do with that.
I was trying to scope the change to exact failure cases to reduce any risk of breaking anything.

I see - I was surprised we'd even get this far with a type that has no bindable members and we're trying to construct with a parameterized constructor.  I would have expected us to discover that in parsing and use a different spec type (not supported or something) - why do we miss this in parsing?

That is because we want use `_typeIndex` which is created and filled in the emitter. If we want to do the detection earlier, we'll need to do more involving refactoring which will make the change risky for 9.0. Note, the parser fills some data structures which expect to see the type specs supported by `_typeIndex` later during the emission. so refactoring will not be simple IMO.

I see - given that it seems like the parser isn't even capable of completely deciding which types will be handled.  It can only decide which *may* be handled and we filter further during emit.  That feels like something we'd need to fix to address other issues.
